option_title: Generative search for single-phase immersion coolants
question: Does verifying more candidate coolants with GPU molecular dynamics keep raising the best figure of merit above known commercial single-phase fluids, or does it plateau?
hypothesis: Predictor-filtered molecular dynamics finds PFAS-free esters or hydrocarbons that beat commercial coolants [orgmol], and more candidates keep improving the best one.

compute_axis.quantity: candidate fluids verified by GPU molecular dynamics

held_fixed: MD simulation length per candidate (12 ns: 2 ns equilibration + 2 x 5 ns production)
temperature 313 K (40 C, the temperature OCP specs k and viscosity at)
force field (united-atom Mie Potoff/TAMie, TraPPE-UA fallback)
molecule class (PFAS-free saturated monoesters and hydrocarbons, <= 30 carbons)
predictor training data and held-out commercial fluids

predictions.if_lever: Best cooling figure of merit keeps climbing with candidates verified, so more compute keeps finding fluids that beat commercial ones.
predictions.if_not: Best figure of merit plateaus by a few hundred candidates, because predictor filtering and ~10% force-field error cap how high MD-ranked fluids score.
predictions.decision_rule: if_lever if the best Mouromtseff number at 1000 candidates exceeds the best at 100 by more than 5% and keeps beating the commercial baseline; if_not if the best plateaus within 5% between 300 and 1000 candidates.
predictions.noise_rule: Run 2 independent replicas per candidate; a level-to-level best-score difference counts only if it exceeds the replica-to-replica standard error of the score.
predictions.expected_why: No published run has MD-verified thousands of immersion-coolant candidates, so whether the hit rate saturates or keeps rising is genuinely unknown.

compute_tested_why: The test varies the number of candidates verified by MD (100 to 1000), which is exactly what more parallel GPUs buy; each candidate is an independent simulation run one-per-GPU.
scored_against: Measured viscosity, thermal conductivity, density, heat capacity and dielectric constant of known commercial fluids (3M Novec 7000 and n-hexadecane), held out of predictor training; never against the predictors.

arms.what: Reproduce n-hexadecane thermal conductivity and viscosity with MD before scoring any candidate
Fine-tune dielectric/viscosity/thermal-conductivity predictors on public data, hold out commercial fluids
Enumerate ~1M PFAS-free esters and hydrocarbons and rank them by predicted figure of merit
MD-verify the next 200 ranked candidates (300 total)
MD-verify the next 700 ranked candidates (1000 total)
Longer 50 ns runs on the top 30 MD-ranked candidates
Compute Mouromtseff numbers and hit rate versus the commercial baseline

baseline.what: Known commercial fluids' published properties converted to a Mouromtseff number: 3M Novec 7000 (k=0.075 W/m/K, 0.32 cSt) and n-hexadecane (k=0.1444 W/m/K, 2.95 mPa s).
baseline.value: k=0.075 W/m/K, nu=0.32 cSt, rho=1400 kg/m3, cp=1300 J/kg/K (Novec 7000); k=0.1444 W/m/K (n-hexadecane)

anchor.what: MD pipeline reproduces n-hexadecane thermal conductivity 0.1444 W/m/K and viscosity 2.95 mPa/s near 300 K before scoring candidates.

checks: Anchor: MD reproduces n-hexadecane k and viscosity within +/-25% before candidates are scored.
Predictor holdout: R^2 >= 0.85 on held-out commercial-fluid properties before trusting the filter.
Score candidates only against measured (never predicted) data for held-out fluids.
Compare each candidate's MD-computed properties, not the predictor's, against the baseline.

phases.what: Build the MD pipeline; reproduce n-hexadecane k and viscosity within +/-25%; measure the real MD throughput.
phases.stop_rule: Stop at the 24 GPU-hour time box or when both properties are within +/-25%.

gate.else: Switch to a Mie (Potoff/TAMie) force field and rerun once; if it still fails, stop before spending on candidates.

phases.what: Fine-tune property predictors (dielectric, viscosity, thermal conductivity) on public data, holding out commercial fluids.
phases.stop_rule: Stop at the 16 GPU-hour time box or when holdout R^2 stops improving.

gate.else: Fall back to a group-contribution ranking as the filter instead of the ML predictor.

phases.what: Enumerate ~1M PFAS-free saturated esters and hydrocarbons, score with the predictor, rank by predicted Mouromtseff number.
phases.stop_rule: Stop when 1M molecules are enumerated and ranked.

gate.else: Relax the dielectric-constant filter and re-rank before starting MD.

phases.what: MD-verify the top 100, then 300, then 1000 candidates (eight A6000s at once), computing density, viscosity, heat capacity and thermal conductivity.
phases.stop_rule: Stop each level when its candidate count is verified or its line's GPU-hours are spent.

phases.what: Compute each candidate's Mouromtseff number and hit rate versus the commercial baseline; apply the decision rule.
phases.stop_rule: Stop when the best-score-versus-candidates curve is plotted at 100/300/1000.

restructuring.sequential_part: One trajectory runs timestep by timestep; verifying a thousand candidates serially chains that work a thousand times.

scope_gap: The 10^4-candidate level is unaffordable, so the curve is only tested to 10^3.
Only pure single-component fluids; mixtures, which the option also names, are not screened.
MD transport properties carry ~10% force-field error, so absolute accuracy is capped even at scale.
No synthesis or experimental validation of the top candidates.

novelty.closest_prior: Org-Mol ML-screened six million esters and experimentally validated two; it never MD-verified hundreds-to-thousands of candidates at once.
novelty.left_open: No study measures whether the best MD-ranked coolant keeps improving as the number of MD-verified candidates grows from 100 to 10,000.

limits: Result is a ranking and hit rate, not absolute fluid accuracy; one fluid class, no mixtures, no synthesis or lifetime testing.
test_summary: Generate a million PFAS-free esters and hydrocarbons, ML-filter to a ranked shortlist, MD-verify the top 100, 300, then 1000 candidates' viscosity and thermal conductivity, and compare their cooling figure of merit to commercial fluids.

sources.quote: we apply the Org-Mol fine-tuned models to systematically screen out promising candidates for immersion coolants, which require low dielectric constant (strictly lower than 3.20 at room temperature for electrical safety), low kinematic viscosity (preferably lower than 12 cSt at 40 °C), high thermal conductivity (preferably higher than 0.140 W/m ⋅ K), and environmental friendliness.
